subject: Hosted inference latency advisory and follow-up
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@brightgrid.com>, BrightGrid Ops <ops@brightgrid.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted inference latency advisory

Hi Samira —

We wanted to let you know we are seeing elevated request latency on our hosted text-generation endpoints (v1/generate and v1/chat) starting ~08:50 PDT. Impact: increased tail latency and intermittent 5xx responses for a subset of requests.

What we know so far:
- Affected scope: hosted API (us-west region), customers on the shared-hosted tier.
- Symptoms: 95th percentile latency spiked from ~180ms to ~2.1s; small fraction (~0.7%) of requests returned 502/504.
- First observed: 2026-09-18 08:50 PDT.

Immediate actions we have taken:
- Throttled non-essential background jobs and ramped up dedicated inference workers in the us-west pool.
- Eng team is investigating an autoscaler interaction that appears to be causing backlog on the request queue.
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/rdw-2026-09-18 (live updates will be posted there).

Estimated next update: within 60–90 minutes. We will keep you posted and follow up with a resolution note and a post-incident summary. If this incident is causing visible customer impact for you, please reply and we will prioritize follow-up.

Attaching an abbreviated snapshot of observed metrics for the last two hours.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, BrightGrid Ops <ops@brightgrid.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted inference latency advisory — update

Samira —

Quick update from the on-call team: engineers have identified a regression in the autoscaler’s job-queue backpressure logic that, under certain load patterns, allowed a backlog to accumulate and then caused large batch retries that saturated worker memory. That led to slow request handling and occasional 5xx for queued requests.

Mitigations applied:
- Rolled back the autoscaler change at 09:58 PDT which stopped the pathological batching.
- Added a temporary request-queue size cap and emergency rate limiting for non-production API keys.
- Prioritized BrightGrid request routing to spare capacity for your traffic pattern (applied at 10:00 PDT).

Current state (10:05 PDT): error rates are down to baseline, p95 latency improving but still elevated for long-running sessions. We expect full normalization within ~2–3 hours as KV caches and worker caches warm and remaining backlog drains.

Support ticket: RDW-5278 (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/tickets/RDW-5278). I’ve attached the incident snapshot and the ticket with engineering notes.

We understand the business impact and will include SLA credit calculations and a full postmortem link in the follow-up.

Ben

Attachments: support_ticket_RDW-5278.txt, incident_snapshot_20260918.json

From: status@status.redwood.ai <status@status.redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@brightgrid.com>, BrightGrid Ops <ops@brightgrid.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 12:34:05 -0700
Subject: [RESOLVED] Incident RDW-2026-09-18 — Hosted inference elevated latency

The incident impacting hosted inference latency in the us-west region has been resolved as of 12:30 PDT. Root cause: autoscaler regression causing backlog and saturation of worker memory.

Impact: increased tail latency and intermittent 5xx between 08:50 and 12:30 PDT.

Corrective actions: rollback of autoscaler change, request-queue cap, emergency rate limiting, and a follow-up postmortem scheduled.

See full incident timeline and updates: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/rdw-2026-09-18
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@brightgrid.com>

Also confirm next steps and timeline for the formal postmortem PDF and whether the credit will be applied to this month’s invoice.

Samira
